title: Two weeks, two job offers: an Opportunity Card story
description: An environmental engineer arrived in Germany on the Opportunity Card and had two offers within a fortnight. How she did it, in her own words.
html:
When an environmental engineer from Lahore landed in Germany with her Opportunity Card, she gave herself twelve months. She needed two weeks. Here is how she describes it.

In her own words

"I had applied to a few jobs from abroad and heard nothing. The moment I had a German address and a German phone number, the same applications started getting replies. Being in the country changes how employers read you."

Treating the search as a job

She worked fixed hours: mornings for applications, afternoons for research and networking, evenings off. She kept a spreadsheet of every application, contact and follow-up. "It sounds boring, but the structure kept me from panicking, and it meant I never forgot to follow up."

Getting past the software

Most large employers run applications through tracking software before a human sees them. She rewrote her CV in the German format, used the exact terms from each job description and kept the layout simple so the software could read it. Interview invitations rose immediately.

The visa conversation

"I explained my status in the first sentence of every interview: I have the Opportunity Card, I can start now, and the company only needs to confirm the contract. Nobody was worried after that. The worry comes when they do not understand the process, so I made sure they did."

Language

Her German was B1 when she arrived. She said so, showed her course enrolment and was hired by a company that works in English but appreciated the effort. "Honesty plus visible progress is worth more than pretending."

Family

She chose between the two offers with her partner's move in mind: the one in a city with a bigger job market for his profession won. "The card gives you a year, but a good decision is one that works for everyone who is coming with you."
